title: fix(dashboard,charts): two declared-translatable dashboard surfaces now resolve (objectui#10132)
body:
Fixes #10132

Clause-②: yes — an exported type of `@object-ui/core` is retyped, and the value vocabulary of a published payload widens. Derived from THIS diff, not from the card. `packages/core/src/index.ts` re-exports both edited modules with `export *`, so everything they export is published. Measured on the built `dist/` tree (the package ships `files: ["dist", …]`), with a negative control in the same command: `DashboardFilterDef` 13 hits, `resolveDashboardFilterDefs` 6, `axisPresentation` 8, and an invented symbol 0 — so the counts are measurements, not a silent instrument. The two moves are (a) `DashboardFilterDef` gains the optional member `object`, present in the shipped `.d.ts` as `object?: string`; (b) `axisPresentation` keeps its signature but may now emit `title` as an inline locale map where it previously always emitted a string. Both are additive: no symbol is removed or renamed, no accept set is relaxed, and no key moves off a payload.

⚠️ The claim comment deliberately carried `Clause-②: pending` and named a `Clause-②-correction:` as the protocol's second carrier — there was no diff yet. This body is the declaration that correction points at, and its value is **yes**.

## Two defects, not one — and they should have been two cards

The card's title joins them and its ⭐ section calls them "one resolver-family fix". Re-derived here, they are not:

| half | what is actually wrong | where the fix lands |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `GlobalFilterSchema.object` | the key is **never read** — no consumer exists at any layer | a carry-through in `@object-ui/core` **plus** two resolver calls in `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` |
| `ChartAxisSchema.title` | the value **bypasses** a resolver that is already downstream of it and already correct | one expression in `@object-ui/core` |

They share no file, no function and no failure mode. Half 1 needed a consumer built from nothing across two packages; half 2 needed one call swapped for its neighbour in the same module, because `normalizeChartSchema` has resolved an axis title through `pickLocalized` against the viewer's language since objectui#8943 — the resolver was never missing, the value just never reached it. ⇒ **they should have been two cards**, and the card's own instinct that "the two halves may not share a fix" was right. They are shipped together here only because they were dispatched together and are individually small; each half's pins, ablation and acceptance stand alone, and either could be reverted without touching the other.

## Both halves reproduce on today's `main`

Nothing was taken on trust; the card's evidence was measured against a pinned published console, this branch re-derived both against `origin/main` at `80c54122e`.

**Half 1.** A `globalFilters[]` entry declaring `object: 'opportunity'`, `field: 'type'` and no `label`, rendered under a bundle that translates it, painted the raw field name `type` and left its option label in the authored English. `resolveDashboardFilterDefs` builds its `DashboardFilterDef` by naming the keys it copies and `object` was not among them, so the value could not reach a renderer even in principle; the only `.object` read anywhere on the filter path was `optionsFrom.object`, which names a different object on purpose.

**Half 2.** `axisPresentation` collapsed an `I18nLabel` axis title with `labelText`, a first-string-in-key-order pick. Both directions measured on one map: written `en` first it painted English to a `zh-CN` viewer; the `en` viewer case was green **against the defect**, which is exactly why a single-language assertion cannot catch this class.

## The resolvers reused — no second one was written

⭐ Both halves call a rung that already existed. Neither fix introduces a resolver, a key convention or a fallback.

- **Half 1, field label** — `useSafeFieldLabel().fieldLabel` from `@object-ui/i18n`, the convention resolver lists and forms already call. It walks the discovered app namespaces for the `fields.OBJECT.FIELD` entry and returns its `fallback` on a miss. Precedence therefore follows the resolver's own signature — the translator's bundle wins, the authored `label` (resolved first, since it may itself be an inline map) is the fallback — so an opted-in filter behaves like every other field label on the console instead of becoming a second precedence rule.
- **Half 1, option labels** — `translateOptions` from the same object, keyed by option value under `fieldOptions.OBJECT.FIELD.VALUE`. ⚠️ Worth stating because the spec's describe text names the family by its FIELD-label key: in this repository the option arm of that same convention is spelled `fieldOptions.…`, and reusing it is what the key's own wording ("zero new i18n vocabulary, one resolver path") asks for. Inventing a second spelling here would have been the second path it forbids.
- **Half 2** — `forwardedI18nLabel`, the neighbour **in the same module**, which already carries a chart's own `title` / `subtitle` / `description` unresolved for precisely this reason (objectui#9038). The map now survives the lowering and `normalizeChartSchema` resolves it, as it always could.

## The objectui#4020 ledger entry that moved, and the one that did not

`chart-presentation.i18nLabel-9038.test.ts` pinned the first-string pick for a series `label` **and** an axis `title` as deliberate, "so a later edit cannot quietly fold them in under this card's banner". This is not quiet. That ledger's justification is "a locale-unaware CHOICE a caller can OVERRIDE" — and it holds for the series label, which `DatasetWidget` replaces from the locale bundle, while nothing overrides an axis title: it is spread onto the chart schema and drawn. So the axis arm was never covered by the reason the pick rests on. `seriesPresentation` keeps the pick and is re-pinned; the moved assertion stays in that same file, rewritten to say which card moved it.

## Lit controls, not absence assertions

"the key is not read" is not observable from one render — a missing translation and an ignored key paint the same pixels. Every pin renders the same surface twice and asserts the two differ.

- `DashboardFilterBar.objectBundleLabel-10132.test.tsx` — the same filter with the bundle entry available and without it: `类型` vs the raw `type`, and `新业务` vs the authored `New business`. Plus an **opt-in control**: a filter with no `object`, against the SAME bundle, must render exactly as today.
- `ChartRenderer.axisTitleLocale-10132.test.tsx` — the same locale map at `zh-CN` and at `en`, through the real `mergeAuthoredPresentation` lowering, spread onto the schema exactly as `DatasetWidget` spreads it. Every map is written `en` FIRST so the `zh-CN` case cannot be satisfied by the first-string pick. Plus a plain-string control and an absence control (an axis with no title draws none, so objectui#9038's erasure mode cannot be mistaken for a pass).
- Seam pins beside each: `dashboard-filters.objectKey-10132.test.ts` and `chart-presentation.axisTitleI18n-10132.test.ts`. Neither half stands alone — a correct seam feeding no consumer is the state this card reports, and a green renderer over a seam that drops the value is the other.

`all-locales-key-parity` is untouched: **no key was added to any locale pack.** Both halves resolve through existing convention resolvers against an app-supplied bundle, so there is nothing for that test to hold to parity.

## Reverse verification

Run from the committed fix, one leg per rung, through `ablation-replace` so the mutation is proven on disk (anchor count, replacement count and the `git hash-object` blob all move) and the restore is proven against `HEAD` rather than against an exit code. ⛔ The tests resolve `@object-ui/core` through the root vitest `resolve.alias` to `packages/core/src`, not to `dist/`, so no stale-build false green is available here.

| leg ablated | outcome |
|:--|:--|
| the `object` carry-through in `resolveDashboardFilterDefs` | 6 failed / 2 passed — both seam and rendered pins red, both controls green |
| `fieldLabel` call in `useFilterLabel` | 2 failed / 2 passed — the two field-label pins red, the option pin still green |
| `translateOptions` call in `SelectFilter` | 1 failed / 3 passed — only the option pin red |
| `forwardedI18nLabel` back to `labelText` in `axisPresentation` | 5 failed / 19 passed — axis seam, the moved ledger assertion and the `zh-CN` render red; the `en` render stayed GREEN, which is the defect's signature |

Each leg restored with `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH`, verified blob-equal to `HEAD` with `git diff HEAD` empty. Working tree clean afterwards, and all pins re-run green from the restored tree.

## Checks on this head

Head `185e950d4`. It is the PR's own tip `bfa70403a`, plus ONE merge of `main` at `ff14e29b5` (`f49ee23c3`; no rebase, no force-push, 154 commits brought in, `git merge-tree` clean), plus one commit from the contract review (below). Updated by the `domain:ui` seat 1, which took over this PR's review and landing on the maintainer's instruction (the takeover record is on this conversation).

- The five pin files: 5 files, 32 tests passed. `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/ packages/plugin-dashboard/ packages/plugin-charts/`: **366 files, 5573 tests, all passed**. The 47 tests that read the touched sources, or those packages' directories, as text: 2445 passed.
- `turbo run build` over the three packages' closure: 12/12. The type-check (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exits 0 for `@object-ui/core`, `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` and `@object-ui/plugin-charts`, and each test program includes its pins.
- All four ablation legs re-run at the merged head. They match the table above exactly: (a) 6 red / 2 green, (b) 2/2, (c) 1/3, (d) 5/19. The controls stay green, and each restore is proven by blob.
- What `main` brought in is disjoint from both halves: objectui#10400 appended `chartTypeIgnoresCompareTo` to `chart-presentation.ts`; objectui#10339 added the date-range default preset in `dashboard-filters.ts`; objectui#9909 and objectui#7495 do not touch the axis or series-label path.
- Gates at this head: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:i18n-keys`, and the doc gates run for the contract-review commit. All exit 0.
- Governed guard over this diff's paths: NOT GOVERNED.

**The contract-review commit (`185e950d4`)** fixes the review's two FAIL items. (1) The changeset grades `@object-ui/core` **`minor`**, because `Clause-②: yes` takes at least `minor`. It was `patch`. (2) `content/docs/guide/dashboard-filters.md` documents `globalFilters[].object` and the i18n precedence it opts into, and `packages/plugin-dashboard/README.md`'s example mirrors it.

## Acceptance notes

Out-of-scope observations, noted and **not** filed — none is a reproducible defect, a breached declared contract, or a trap that makes an author write metadata the runtime refuses:

- `labelText` in `chart-presentation.ts` now has exactly one caller left (`seriesPresentation`). Its first-string pick is still ledgered under objectui#4020 and still has the overriding caller that justifies it, so this is an observation about shrinkage, not a defect. Who would meet it: the next card that touches objectui#4020's ledger. noted, not filed.
- The spec's describe text for `GlobalFilterSchema.object` says the option labels resolve "through the SAME `fields.OBJECT.FIELD` convention", while this repository's option arm of that convention is keyed `fieldOptions.OBJECT.FIELD.VALUE`. The two agree on the family and disagree on the spelling of one arm. That is a wording question on a contract owned by another repository, ⛔ not this lane's to change, and the behaviour here matches what lists and forms do. Carrier: whoever next edits that describe text. noted, not filed.
- `DashboardWidgetInspector` in `@object-ui/app-shell` is `resolveDashboardFilterDefs`' other caller and renders filter labels of its own. It is unaffected (the new member is optional and additive) but it does not resolve the bundle either, so a designer preview will keep showing the authored label where the runtime now shows the translation. Not filed: it is a preview surface, the divergence is pre-existing for every other convention-resolved label there, and widening this card to cover it was not dispatched. Carrier: a designer-preview i18n card, if one is ever opened. noted, not filed.
